1.solution:
Kinetic energy \(K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}\), so fractional errors add with the powers:
\[\frac{\Delta K}{K}\times100 = \frac{\Delta m}{m}\times100 + 2\frac{\Delta v}{v}\times100 = 3\% + 2(4\%) = 11\%.\]

2.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
2.solution:
For a banked road with the same banking angle and friction, the maximum safe speed \(v_{\max}\propto\sqrt{r}\). Hence \(\dfrac{r_{2}}{r_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{v_{2}}{v_{1}}\right)^{2}\). With \(v_{2}=1.2v_{1}\) and \(r_{1}=20\,\text{m}\):
\[r_{2} = (1.2)^{2}\times20 = 28.8\,\text{m}.\]
Increase in radius \(= 28.8 - 20 = 8.8\,\text{m}\).

3.solution:
A ball rolling in a curved surface of radius of curvature \(R\) behaves like a particle on a track of effective radius \((R-r)\). The restoring force gives \(\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{R-r}}\), so
\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R-r}{g}} \propto \sqrt{\frac{R-r}{g}}.\]

4.solution:
Three equal charges at the vertices of an equilateral triangle form 3 equal pairs:
\[U_{net} = 3\times\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}}\frac{q^{2}}{l} = 3\times9\times10^{9}\times\frac{(3\times10^{-6})^{2}}{6\times10^{-2}}.\]
\[= 3\times9\times10^{9}\times\frac{9\times10^{-12}}{6\times10^{-2}} = 4.05\,\text{J} \approx 4.1\,\text{J}.\]

5.subtopic: Classification, Curie's Law, Hysteresis, and Shielding
5.solution: Magnetic hysteresis (a B-H loop with retentivity and coercivity) is a characteristic of ferromagnetic materials only; paramagnetic and diamagnetic materials do not show hysteresis.

7.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
7.solution:
Apparent power \(= V_{rms}I_{rms}\), true power \(= V_{rms}I_{rms}\cos\phi\). Their ratio is \(\dfrac{1}{\cos\phi}\). Since \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{R}{Z}\),
\[\frac{\text{apparent power}}{\text{true power}} = \frac{1}{\cos\phi} = \frac{Z}{R}.\]

8.solution: From the figure, B and C feed a NOR gate giving \(\overline{B+C}\), which is then ANDed with A: \(Y = A\cdot\overline{B+C}\). This is HIGH only when \(A=1\) and \(\overline{B+C}=1\), i.e. \(B=0\) and \(C=0\).

9.subtopic: Kinematics — Equations of Motion, Free Fall, and Graphs

10.solution: In \(A\to B+\,_{2}He^{4}\) (alpha decay), Z decreases by 2 and A by 4. In \(B\to C+2e^{-}\) (two beta-minus decays), Z increases by 2 while A is unchanged. So A and C have the same atomic number (Z) but different mass numbers \((A,\,A-4)\) — they are isotopes.

11.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
11.solution:
From the figure, axis \(XX'\) lies along the diameter of the semicircular ring. A semicircular arc and a full ring have the same MI about a diameter since all mass is at radius \(R\); MI about a diameter is \(I = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2}\). With \(L = \pi R \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{L}{\pi}\),
\[I = \frac{M}{2}\left(\frac{L}{\pi}\right)^{2} = \frac{ML^{2}}{2\pi^{2}}.\]

12.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
12.solution:
Speed at displacement \(x\): \(u = \omega\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}\). Maximum speed \(V_{\max} = \omega a\). Given \(u = \dfrac{V_{\max}}{2} = \dfrac{\omega a}{2}\):
\[\frac{\omega a}{2} = \omega\sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}} \Rightarrow a^{2}-x^{2} = \frac{a^{2}}{4} \Rightarrow x = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}a.\]

13.solution: Each of the \(n\) identical capacitors holds charge \(Q = CV\). When reconnected in series, the same charge flows and the potential differences add: total p.d. \(= nV\). The stored energy is conserved (no resistive path), so it remains the same.

14.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
14.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
14.solution: For the \(n\)th Bohr orbit, the circumference equals \(n\) de Broglie wavelengths: \(2\pi r = n\lambda\), so \(\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi r}{n}\). Since \(r \propto n^{2}\), \(\lambda \propto \dfrac{n^{2}}{n} = n\). Thus \(\lambda \propto n\).

15.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks

16.solution:
Balancing length is proportional to the emf being balanced. \(E_{1}\propto l_{1}\). When the cells oppose, the net emf \((E_{1}-E_{2})\propto l_{2}\). Hence \(E_{2} = k(l_{1}-l_{2})\) and
\[\frac{E_{1}}{E_{2}} = \frac{kl_{1}}{k(l_{1}-l_{2})} = \frac{l_{1}}{l_{1}-l_{2}}.\]
16.note: Stem prints the opposing balancing length again as l_1; from the AK working it is l_2 (the second/opposing balance length).

17.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
17.solution: Magnetic flux \(\phi = LI\), so on a \(\phi\)-vs-\(I\) graph the self-inductance \(L\) is the slope. From the figure, line \(P\) has the steepest slope, so it has the largest self-inductance.

19.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion

20.solution:
From the figure the two cells (200 V and 10 V) oppose each other in the loop with a \(38\,\Omega\) resistor: net emf \(= 200 - 10 = 190\,\text{V}\).
\[I = \frac{V_{eq}}{R} = \frac{190}{38} = 5\,\text{A}.\]

21.subtopic: Gravitational PE, Escape Velocity, and Energy
21.solution:
Magnitude of PE at distance \(R\): \(\dfrac{GMm}{R} = E\), so \(GMm = ER\). Weight at \(1.5R\):
\[W = \frac{GMm}{(1.5R)^{2}} = \frac{ER}{2.25R^{2}} = \frac{E}{2.25R} = \frac{4E}{9R}.\]

22.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
22.subtopic: de Broglie Wavelength and Matter Waves
22.solution:
For a thermal neutron \(\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}\) with \(v\propto\sqrt{T}\), so \(\lambda\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{T}}\).
\[\frac{\lambda_{927}}{\lambda_{27}} = \sqrt{\frac{27+273}{927+273}} = \sqrt{\frac{300}{1200}} = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \lambda_{927} = \frac{\lambda_{0}}{2}.\]

23.solution:
Sphere: \(V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^{3}\), \(A = 4\pi R^{2}\), so \(\dfrac{V}{A} = \dfrac{R}{3} \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{3V}{A}\). Capacitance of an isolated sphere:
\[C = 4\pi\varepsilon_{0}R = 4\pi\varepsilon_{0}\cdot\frac{3V}{A} = \frac{12\pi\varepsilon_{0}V}{A}.\]

24.subtopic: SHM Kinematics — Displacement, Velocity, Phase, and Damping
24.solution:
\(T = 8\,\text{s} \Rightarrow \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}\,\text{rad/s}\). Starting at mean position, \(x = A\sin\omega t\).
\(x(1) = A\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\) (distance in 1st second).
\(x(2) = A\sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = A\), so distance in 2nd second \(= A - \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\).
\[\text{ratio} = \frac{A/\sqrt{2}}{A(1-1/\sqrt{2})} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}-1} = 1:(\sqrt{2}-1).\]

25.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
25.solution:
Energy = surface tension times increase in surface area: \(W = T\left(n\cdot4\pi r^{2} - 4\pi R^{2}\right)\). Volume conservation gives \(n = \dfrac{R^{3}}{r^{3}}\):
\[W = 4\pi T\left(\frac{R^{3}}{r^{3}}r^{2} - R^{2}\right) = 4\pi T R^{2}\left(\frac{R}{r}-1\right).\]

26.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
26.solution: For a pipe closed at one end the \(p\)th mode is \(n_{p} = (2p-1)\dfrac{v}{4L}\). The second overtone is the 3rd mode (5th harmonic), which has 3 nodes and 3 antinodes.

27.solution:
In steady state \(\dfrac{Q}{t} = KA\dfrac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{x}\). Solving for the conductivity,
\[K = \frac{xQ}{tA(T_{1}-T_{2})}.\]

28.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
28.subtopic: Force on Moving Charge in Magnetic Field

29.solution: A Zener diode regulates voltage in the reverse breakdown region, where the voltage stays nearly constant while current varies. From the figure this is the steep reverse-bias portion \(de\).

30.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
30.solution:
Excess pressure in a soap bubble \(P = \dfrac{4T}{r}\), so \(P\propto\dfrac{1}{r}\). Given \(P_{1} = 1.5P_{2}\Rightarrow \dfrac{r_{2}}{r_{1}} = 1.5\). Volume ratio:
\[x = \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} = \left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)^{3} = (1.5)^{3} = \frac{27}{8}.\]

31.solution: Frequency is inversely proportional to length (tension fixed): \(n_{2}l_{2} = n_{1}l_{1}\). With \(l_{2} = 1.25l_{1}\), \(n_{2} = \dfrac{n_{1}}{1.25} = 0.8n_{1}\), i.e. a 20% decrease. The second harmonic scales the same way, so it decreases by 20%.

32.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
32.solution:
For the \(n\)th secondary maximum \(a\sin\theta = \left(n+\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda\); for the second maximum \(n=2\Rightarrow a\dfrac{y}{D} = \dfrac{5}{2}\lambda\).
\[\lambda = \frac{2ay}{5D} = \frac{2\times0.65\times10^{-3}\times2.6\times10^{-3}}{5\times1.3} = 5.2\times10^{-7}\,\text{m} = 5200\,\text{\AA}.\]

33.subtopic: Doppler Effect — Moving Source and Observer
33.solution: When source and observer approach each other, \(n = n_{0}\dfrac{v+v_{o}}{v-v_{s}} > n_{0}\): the apparent frequency increases. Since \(\lambda = \dfrac{v}{n}\), the wavelength decreases. So: high frequency, low wavelength.

34.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
34.solution: Capillary rise \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}\), and mass \(m = \rho\cdot\pi r^{2}h = \dfrac{2\pi T\cos\theta}{g}\,r\). Thus \(m\propto r\). For radius \(\dfrac{r}{5}\), the mass becomes \(\dfrac{m}{5}\).

35.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
35.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
35.solution: Torque \(\tau = IAB\sin\theta \propto A\). For wires of equal length (equal perimeter), a circular loop encloses a larger area than a square. Hence the circular loop experiences the greater torque.

36.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
36.subtopic: Force on Current-Carrying Conductor and Parallel Wires
36.note: Option D as printed reads sqrt(2) I L B (the B_0 subscript dropped in extraction); it is sqrt(2) I L B_0.

37.subtopic: Lenses — Lens Formula, Power, and Lensmaker
37.solution:
Lens maker in a medium: \(\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\dfrac{n_{lens}}{n_{med}}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_{1}}-\dfrac{1}{R_{2}}\right)\). For a biconcave lens \(R_{1}=-R,\,R_{2}=+R\), so \(\left(\dfrac{1}{R_{1}}-\dfrac{1}{R_{2}}\right) = -\dfrac{2}{R}\).
\[\frac{1}{f} = \left(\frac{1.5}{1.75}-1\right)\left(-\frac{2}{R}\right) = \left(-\frac{1}{7}\right)\left(-\frac{2}{R}\right) = \frac{2}{7R} \Rightarrow f = +3.5R.\]
Positive focal length means it behaves as a convex lens of focal length \(3.5R\).

38.subtopic: Gas Laws and Ideal Gas Equation
38.solution:
At constant volume \(P\propto T\). A pressure increase of 2.5% gives \(P_{2} = 1.025P_{1}\):
\[\frac{P_{1}}{1.025P_{1}} = \frac{T_{1}}{T_{1}+4} \Rightarrow T_{1}+4 = 1.025T_{1} \Rightarrow 0.025T_{1} = 4 \Rightarrow T_{1} = 160\,\text{K}.\]
38.note: Stem prints '2.3%'; the keyed answer 160 K requires a 2.5% increase (4/0.025 = 160), and the AK solution itself uses 2.5%. A 2.3% increase would give 173.9 K, which is not an option. Corrected to 2.5%.
38.stemOverride: When the pressure of the gas contained in a closed vessel is increased by \(2.5\%\), the temperature of the gas increases by 4 K . The initial temperature of the gas is

39.solution: Optical path through a film of thickness \(t\) and refractive index \(n\) is \(nt\), replacing the geometric path \(t\). The increase is \(nt - t = (n-1)t\).

40.subtopic: RMS, Peak, and AC Source Characteristics
40.solution:
\(\dfrac{e_{0}}{2} = e_{0}\sin\omega t \Rightarrow \sin\omega t = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \omega t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\). With \(\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}\):
\[\frac{2\pi}{T}t = \frac{\pi}{6} \Rightarrow t = \frac{T}{12}.\]

41.solution:
Total flux from the charge \(= \dfrac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}}\), shared equally among 6 faces, so one face has \(\dfrac{Q}{6\varepsilon_{0}}\). Two opposite faces give
\[2\times\frac{Q}{6\varepsilon_{0}} = \frac{Q}{3\varepsilon_{0}}.\]

42.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
42.solution:
Fundamentals of open pipes: \(n = \dfrac{v}{2L}\), \(n' = \dfrac{v}{2(L+L_{1})}\). Beat frequency:
\[n-n' = \frac{v}{2}\left(\frac{1}{L}-\frac{1}{L+L_{1}}\right) = \frac{vL_{1}}{2L(L+L_{1})}.\]

43.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
43.solution:
Wien's law: \(\lambda T = \text{const}\), so \(\lambda_{A}T_{A} = \lambda_{B}T_{B}\). With \(T_{A} = 3T_{B}\), \(\lambda_{B} = 3\lambda_{A}\). Given \(\lambda_{B}-\lambda_{A} = 4\,\mu\text{m}\):
\[3\lambda_{A}-\lambda_{A} = 4 \Rightarrow \lambda_{A} = 2\,\mu\text{m},\quad \lambda_{B} = 6\,\mu\text{m}.\]
43.note: Stem dropped the wavelength-difference value; from the AK solution it is 4 micrometre.
43.stemOverride: Black bodies A and B radiate maximum energy with wavelength difference \(4\mu\text{ }m\). The absolute temperature of body A is 3 times that of B . The wavelength at which body B radiates maximum energy is

44.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
44.solution:
Adiabatic: \(TV^{\gamma-1} = \text{const}\), so \(\dfrac{T_{2}}{T_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma-1}\). For a monoatomic gas \(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\Rightarrow\gamma-1 = \dfrac{2}{3}\). With \(V = AL\):
\[\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}} = \left(\frac{L_{1}}{L_{2}}\right)^{2/3}.\]

45.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
45.solution: Inductive reactance \(X_{L} = \omega L = 2\pi f L\). For d.c. \(f = 0\Rightarrow X_{L} = 0\); for a.c. \(X_{L}\neq0\). Thus \(\dfrac{X_{ac}}{X_{dc}} = \dfrac{X_{ac}}{0} = \infty\).

46.subtopic: Band Theory, Doping, and Semiconductor Types
46.solution: In an n-type semiconductor, donor impurity atoms create donor energy levels in the band gap just below (close to) the conduction band, so little energy is needed to promote those electrons into the conduction band.

47.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
47.solution:
Equal radiated power per unit area: \(e_{1}\sigma T_{1}^{4} = e_{2}\sigma T_{2}^{4}\). With \(\dfrac{e_{1}}{e_{2}} = \dfrac{16}{1}\):
\[\left(\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}\right)^{4} = \frac{e_{2}}{e_{1}} = \frac{1}{16} \Rightarrow \frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}} = \frac{1}{2} = 0.5.\]
Since \(T_{1} = xT_{2}\), \(x = 0.5\).

48.solution: Crossed polaroids (1 and 2 at \(90^{\circ}\)); a third at angle \(\theta\) to the first is inserted between. After P1: \(I_{1} = \dfrac{I_{0}}{2}\). After P3: \(I_{2} = \dfrac{I_{0}}{2}\cos^{2}\theta\). After P2 (at \(90^{\circ}-\theta\) to P3): \(I_{3} = \dfrac{I_{0}}{2}\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{I_{0}}{8}\sin^{2}2\theta\).

49.subtopic: Series LCR — Impedance, Phase, and Resonance
49.solution: Adding a capacitor in series with an LR circuit introduces \(X_{C}\), which partly cancels \(X_{L}\). The net impedance \(Z = \sqrt{R^{2}+(X_{L}-X_{C})^{2}}\) decreases (toward resonance), so the alternating current increases.

50.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
50.solution:
Isobaric: \(Q = nC_{p}\Delta T\), \(\Delta U = nC_{v}\Delta T\), \(W = Q-\Delta U = n(C_{p}-C_{v})\Delta T\).
\[\frac{Q}{W} = \frac{C_{p}}{C_{p}-C_{v}} = \frac{C_{p}/C_{v}}{(C_{p}-C_{v})/C_{v}} = \frac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}.\]
For a monoatomic check (\(\gamma = 5/3\)): \(\dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma-1} = 2.5\), and directly \(\dfrac{Q}{W} = \dfrac{C_{p}}{R} = \dfrac{(5/2)R}{R} = 2.5\). So \(\dfrac{Q}{W} = \dfrac{\gamma}{\gamma-1}\), which is option C.
50.note: Q/W = C_p/(C_p - C_v) = gamma/(gamma - 1), which is option C. The AK's own solution derives gamma/(gamma - 1) but keyed D ((gamma - 1)/gamma, the reciprocal). Numeric check (monoatomic): Q/W = 2.5 = gamma/(gamma-1), not 0.4. Correct answer C; option C exists so not flawed.

51.solution: A conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one proton: the acid has one more \(\mathrm{H^+}\) than its conjugate base. In \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-} + H_3O^{+} \rightleftharpoons H_2SO_3 + H_2O}\), \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-}}\) accepts a proton to become \(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\); so \(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\) (acid) and \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-}}\) (base) form a conjugate pair.

52.solution: Reactivity in aromatic nucleophilic substitution increases with the number of strong electron-withdrawing groups at the ortho/para positions, which stabilise the carbanion (Meisenheimer) intermediate. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene has three \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) groups at o/p positions, so it is the most reactive.

53.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
53.solution: A Grignard reagent adds to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and after acidic work-up gives a carboxylic acid with one more carbon than the alkyl group. \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHMgBr}\) (isopropyl) gives \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}COOH}\), i.e. 2-methylpropanoic acid (isobutyric acid).

54.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
54.solution: The electrode with the higher (less negative) reduction potential is the cathode. \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode} = E^{\circ}_{Sn} - E^{\circ}_{Fe} = (-0.14) - (-0.44) = +0.30\ \mathrm{V}\).

55.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
55.solution: Number of electrons in antibonding MOs: \(\mathrm{Li_2}\) has 2 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2\); \(\mathrm{N_2}\) has 4; \(\mathrm{O_2}\) has 6 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2(\sigma^{*}2s)^2(\pi^{*}2p)^2\); \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has 8 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2(\sigma^{*}2s)^2(\pi^{*}2p)^4\). \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has the maximum.

56.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
56.solution: Pressure-volume work \(W = -\Delta n_g RT\); it is negative when \(\Delta n_g > 0\) (gas expands). For \(\mathrm{2H_2O_2(l) \to 2H_2O(l) + O_2(g)}\), \(\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = +1\), so \(W = -RT < 0\). The other reactions have \(\Delta n_g \le 0\) (gas moles decrease), giving zero or positive work.

57.solution: Packing efficiency of an fcc cell is \(74\%\) for the 4 atoms it contains. Volume occupied by one atom \(= \dfrac{0.74}{4} \times (1.6\times 10^{-23}) = 0.185 \times 1.6\times 10^{-23} = 2.96\times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
57.stemOverride: Calculate the volume occupied by a particle in fcc unit cell if volume of unit cell is \(1.6 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
57.note: Stem cell volume lost its leading digit in extraction ('.6' \(\to\) intended \(1.6\times10^{-23}\)); restored so the answer \(2.96\times10^{-24}\) (= 0.74/4 \(\times\) cell volume) is reproducible. Key B correct.

58.solution: Alanine has the structure \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(NH_2){-}COOH}\); its side chain is \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\). Leucine has an isobutyl side chain, serine \(-\mathrm{CH_2OH}\), and valine an isopropyl side chain.

59.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
59.solution: Curcumin, the active constituent of turmeric, is well known for its antiseptic property.

60.solution: Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. Mg (period 3, group 2) is smallest; Na > Mg; K is below Na; Rb is below K. Increasing order: \(\mathrm{Mg < Na < K < Rb}\).
60.stemOverride: Which is the correct increasing order of atomic radii of Na, K, Mg, Rb?
60.note: Stem element 'a' is a dropped 'Na'; restored. Key B correct.

61.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
61.solution: First ionisation enthalpies (kJ/mol): La \(\approx 538\), Ce \(\approx 534\), Gd \(\approx 593\), Yb \(\approx 603\). The relatively high value of Yb arises from its filled \(4f^{14}\) configuration. Hence Yb has the highest \(IE_1\).

62.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
62.solution: Carboxylic acids react with \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) to give the acid chloride along with \(\mathrm{POCl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\): \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH + PCl_5 \to C_6H_5COCl + POCl_3 + HCl}\). The reagent is \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\).

63.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
63.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Al \to Al^{3+}(0.1\,M) + 3e^{-}}\), the standard oxidation potential is \(+1.66\ \mathrm{V}\). By Nernst, \(E = E^{\circ}_{ox} - \dfrac{0.0592}{3}\log[\mathrm{Al^{3+}}] = 1.66 - \dfrac{0.0592}{3}\log(0.1) = 1.66 - 0.0197(-1) = 1.66 + 0.0197 = +1.679\ \mathrm{V}\).

64.solution: For a 1:4 mass ratio of \(\mathrm{O_2:CH_4}\), molecules \(\propto\) moles \(= \dfrac{\text{mass}}{M}\). \(\dfrac{N_{O_2}}{N_{CH_4}} = \dfrac{1/32}{4/16} = \dfrac{1/32}{1/4} = \dfrac{1}{8}\). Ratio \(= 1:8\).

65.solution: Relative lowering of vapour pressure \(= \dfrac{W_2 M_1}{M_2 W_1} = \dfrac{3 \times 18}{60 \times 50} = \dfrac{54}{3000} = 0.018\).

66.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
66.solution: Brass is an alloy of Cu and Zn in which Zn atoms (similar size to Cu) replace Cu atoms at lattice sites. This is a substitutional impurity defect.

67.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
67.solution: Azo coupling is the reaction of a diazonium salt with an electron-rich arene (phenol or aromatic amine) to give an azo compound. Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol to give p-hydroxyazobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}N{=}N{-}C_6H_4OH}\)).

68.subtopic: Nomenclature, Structural Isomers and Physical Properties
68.solution: Undecane \((\mathrm{C_{11}H_{24}})\) and decane \((\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}})\) are successive members of the alkane homologous series, differing by one \(-\mathrm{CH_2}-\) unit, i.e. \(14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\).

69.subtopic: Polyhalogen Compounds — Freon, DDT, War Gases
69.solution: BHC (benzene hexachloride, gammexane/lindane) is an effective insecticide used in place of DDT.

70.solution: Atomic ratio \(\mathrm{Xe:F} = 0.4:2.4 = 1:6\), so the compound is \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\). With F as \(-1\): \(x + 6(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6\).

71.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation

72.subtopic: Nomenclature, Hybridization and Stability of Alkenes
72.solution: Cis-trans isomerism requires each doubly-bonded carbon to bear two different groups. In but-1-ene \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}CH{=}CH_2}\) the terminal carbon has two identical H atoms, so no geometric isomerism. But-2-ene, pent-2-ene and 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene all show cis-trans isomerism.

73.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
73.solution: Reduction of a nitrile with DIBAL-H \((\mathrm{AlH(i\text{-}Bu)_2})\) followed by hydrolysis gives an aldehyde with the same carbon skeleton. Pent-3-enal \(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_2CHO}\) therefore comes from pent-3-enenitrile \(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_2C{\equiv}N}\).

74.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
74.solution: Benzene-1,4-diol (hydroquinone) is commonly called quinol. (Catechol = 1,2-diol; resorcinol = 1,3-diol; pyrogallol = 1,2,3-triol.)

75.solution: In a halous acid the halogen is in the \(+3\) oxidation state. For chlorine this is chlorous acid, \(\mathrm{HClO_2}\).

76.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy

77.solution: Number of atoms in mass \(x = \dfrac{x \cdot n}{\rho a^3}\). For fcc, \(n = 4\). Atoms in 1 g \(= \dfrac{1 \times 4}{6.8\times 10^{-22}} = 5.882\times 10^{21}\).

78.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
78.solution: In sucrose the glycosidic bond forms between C-1 of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose (anomeric/aldehyde carbon) and C-2 of \(\beta\)-D-fructose (anomeric/keto carbon). So the carbons are C-1 and C-2 respectively.

79.subtopic: Oxidation State, Coordination Number and IUPAC Nomenclature
79.solution: An octahedral complex has six ligand donor atoms around the central metal ion, so the coordination number is 6 (\(d^2sp^3\) or \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation).

80.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
80.solution: For \(\mathrm{2NO + 2H_2 \to N_2 + 2H_2O}\), rate \(= -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\). Hence \(\dfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}\), which is option B.

82.solution: In a haloalkyne the halogen is bonded to an sp-hybridised carbon of the triple bond (e.g. \(\mathrm{X{-}C{\equiv}C{-}R}\)). Hence the halogen is on an sp carbon.

83.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
83.solution: Catechol is the 1,2-dihydroxybenzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,2-diol.

84.solution: Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, can show only the \(-1\) oxidation state in compounds with oxygen and forms a single oxoacid, hypofluorous acid \(\mathrm{HOF}\). Chlorine shows multiple positive oxidation states (\(+1,+3,+5,+7\)) and forms four oxoacids: \(\mathrm{HOCl, HClO_2, HClO_3, HClO_4}\) — the maximum number. Hence Cl forms the maximum number of oxoacids.
84.note: AK key A (F) is wrong and contradicts standard chemistry. Fluorine forms only ONE oxoacid (HOF), the fewest of all halogens, because it cannot take positive oxidation states. Chlorine forms FOUR oxoacids (HOCl, HClO2, HClO3, HClO4) — the maximum. Correct answer is B (Cl).

85.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
85.solution: First law: \(\Delta U = Q + W\). Work done on the system \(W = +20\ \mathrm{kJ}\); heat released by the system \(Q = -10\ \mathrm{kJ}\). \(\Delta U = -10 + 20 = +10\ \mathrm{kJ}\).

86.solution: \(\Delta T_b = i K_b m\); with \(K_b\) constant, compare \(i\,m\): KCl \(2\times0.2 = 0.4\); NaCl \(2\times0.1 = 0.2\); \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) \(4\times1 = 4\); \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) \(3\times0.05 = 0.15\). The minimum \(i\,m\) (0.15, for \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\)) gives the minimum boiling-point elevation.

87.solution: Neoprene is polychloroprene, the addition polymer of chloroprene, 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene.

88.solution: Carbonyl (CO) is a neutral ligand. Sulphato \((\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}})\), oxalato \((\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}})\) and bromo \((\mathrm{Br^{-}})\) are anionic ligands.

89.solution: The Fischer-Tropsch synthesis of gasoline from water gas uses a cobalt-thoria (Co-Th, with kieselguhr) catalyst.

90.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
90.solution: Overall order is the sum of the exponents in the rate law: \(1.5 + 2.5 = 4\).

91.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
91.solution: By the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion increases with the magnitude of its charge opposite to the sol. For a positive sol, the most negatively charged anion is most effective. \([\mathrm{Fe(CN)_6}]^{4-}\) (charge \(-4\)) has the highest coagulating power.

92.solution: An allylic halide has X on the \(sp^3\) carbon directly adjacent to a \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\). In A, B and C the \(\mathrm{CH_2{-}X}\) is next to the double bond (allylic). In D, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}X}\), the C bearing X is two carbons from the double bond (homoallylic), so it is NOT an allylic halide.

93.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
93.solution: Aniline with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}\) at 273 K gives benzenediazonium chloride (A). On warming with water it hydrolyses, releasing \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and giving phenol (B): \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^{+}Cl^{-} + H_2O \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_5OH + N_2 + HCl}\).

94.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
94.solution: The strongest oxidising agent has the highest standard reduction potential and the greatest tendency to be reduced. \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has the highest \(E^{\circ}\) among the species, so it is the strongest oxidising agent.

95.subtopic: Subatomic Particles, Isotopes, Isobars and Isoelectronic Species
95.solution: Isoelectronic species have the same number of electrons. Ne has 10 electrons and \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\) (8 + 2) also has 10, so they are isoelectronic.

96.solution: \(m = \dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b} = \dfrac{0.6}{2} = 0.3\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}\). Since \(m = \dfrac{\text{moles solute}}{\text{mass solvent (kg)}}\), mass of solvent \(= \dfrac{0.01}{0.3} = 0.033\ \mathrm{kg}\).

97.solution: The \(-\mathrm{CO{-}NH}-\) (amide) linkage is present in urea-formaldehyde resin \((\mathrm{[-NH{-}CO{-}NH{-}CH_2-]_n})\). Glyptal (polyester), thermocol (polystyrene) and Buna-N (copolymer of butadiene and acrylonitrile) lack the amide linkage.

98.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
98.solution: Highest \(pK_b\) means the weakest base. In aniline \((\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2})\) the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, reducing its availability, so aniline is the weakest base and has the highest \(pK_b\).

99.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
99.solution: For first order, \(k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}\), so \(k \propto \dfrac{1}{t_{1/2}}\). With \((t_{1/2})_A = 75\ \mathrm{min}\) and \((t_{1/2})_B = 2.5\ \mathrm{h} = 150\ \mathrm{min}\), the ratio of rate constants \(= \dfrac{(t_{1/2})_B}{(t_{1/2})_A} = \dfrac{150}{75} = 2.0\). Among the options only 2.0 is consistent with the intended computation.
99.note: Stem labels the asked ratio as r_B/r_A but the AK solution computes 150/75 = 2 (which is k_A/k_B). The literal k_B/k_A = 0.5 is not among the options; the intended value, 2.0 (option A), is the only viable choice, so the answer is A. Printed-paper labelling inconsistency, not a key error.

100.solution: Moles in 1 mL \((=10^{-3}\ \mathrm{L})\) of vapour at STP \(= \dfrac{10^{-3}}{22.4} = 4.46\times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{mol}\). Molecules \(= 4.46\times 10^{-5} \times 6.022\times 10^{23} = 2.69\times 10^{19}\).

101.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometry — Identities, Equations, and Principal Values

102.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
102.solution: The given line has direction ratios \((3,-2,1)\). Line \(L\) is parallel to it through \((1,2,3)\): \(\dfrac{x-1}3=\dfrac{y-2}{-2}=\dfrac{z-3}1=\mu\), so a general point is \((3\mu+1,-2\mu+2,\mu+3)\). For \((-5,6,2)\): \(3\mu+1=-5\Rightarrow\mu=-2\) and \(-2\mu+2=6\Rightarrow\mu=-2\), but \(\mu+3=2\Rightarrow\mu=-1\neq-2\). Hence \(L\) does not pass through \((-5,6,2)\).

103.solution: Normal \(=(\hat i+\hat j+\hat k)\times(\hat i-2\hat j+3\hat k)=5\hat i-2\hat j-3\hat k\). The plane passes through \((1,-1,0)\): \(5(x-1)-2(y+1)-3z=0\Rightarrow5x-2y-3z=7\). Distance from origin \(=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{25+4+9}}=\dfrac7{\sqrt{38}}\) units.

104.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions
104.solution: Line direction \((1,2,\lambda)\), plane normal \((1,2,3)\). \(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|1+4+3\lambda|}{\sqrt{5+\lambda^2}\sqrt{14}}\). Given \(\cos\theta=\sqrt{\tfrac5{14}}\Rightarrow\sin\theta=\dfrac3{\sqrt{14}}\). So \(\dfrac{5+3\lambda}{\sqrt{14}\sqrt{5+\lambda^2}}=\dfrac3{\sqrt{14}}\Rightarrow5+3\lambda=3\sqrt{5+\lambda^2}\). Squaring: \(9\lambda^2+30\lambda+25=45+9\lambda^2\Rightarrow30\lambda=20\Rightarrow\lambda=\dfrac23\).

106.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
106.solution: G.P. condition: \(\cos^2\theta=\dfrac16\sin\theta\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{6\cos\theta}\Rightarrow6\cos^3\theta=\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta\). So \(6\cos^3\theta+\cos^2\theta-1=0=(\cos\theta-\tfrac12)(6\cos^2\theta+4\cos\theta+2)\). Only real root \(\cos\theta=\dfrac12\Rightarrow\theta=2n\pi\pm\dfrac{\pi}3\).

107.subtopic: Rolle's Theorem and Mean Value Theorem
107.solution: By Lagrange's MVT, \(\dfrac{f(5)-f(1)}{5-1}=f'(c)\le5\Rightarrow f(5)-1\le20\Rightarrow f(5)\le21\). Maximum value is \(21\).

108.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
108.solution: \(\cot\dfrac A2=\dfrac{b+c}a=\dfrac{\sin B+\sin C}{\sin A}\). Using sum-to-product, \(\dfrac{\cos(A/2)}{\sin(A/2)}=\dfrac{2\sin\frac{B+C}2\cos\frac{B-C}2}{2\sin\frac A2\cos\frac A2}\Rightarrow\cos\dfrac A2=\cos\dfrac{B-C}2\Rightarrow A=B-C\). With \(A+B+C=\pi\), \(2B=\pi\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{\pi}2\): right angled.

109.solution: From \(AA^{-1}=I\), equating entries of \(\dfrac1{11}\) times the product to \(I\): \(15b=0\Rightarrow b=0\); \(2-3a=11\Rightarrow a=-3\); \(24-24c=0\Rightarrow c=1\). So \((a,b,c)=(-3,0,1)\).

110.solution: A statement and its contrapositive have the same truth value. \(p\): "7 odd \(\to\) 7 divisible by 2" \(\equiv T\to F\equiv F\), so \(V_1=F\). \(q\): "7 prime \(\to\) 7 odd" \(\equiv T\to T\equiv T\), so \(V_2=T\). Hence \((V_1,V_2)=(F,T)\).

111.solution: \(\log_3 3x=1+\log_3 x\); as \(x\to1\), \(\log_3 x\to0\), a \(1^\infty\) form. \(\left(1+\dfrac{\log x}{\log3}\right)^{\frac{\log8}{\log x}}\to e^{\frac{\log x}{\log3}\cdot\frac{\log8}{\log x}}=e^{\frac{\log8}{\log3}}=e^{\log_3 8}\).

113.subtopic: Inverse, Composite, and Special Function Equations

114.solution: Put \(t=x^2\): \(I=\dfrac12\int\dfrac{t\,dt}{(t+1)(t+4)}\). Partial fractions give \(\dfrac{-1}{3(t+1)}+\dfrac{4}{3(t+4)}\). Integrating and back-substituting, \(I=\dfrac13\log\dfrac{(x^2+4)^2}{\sqrt{x^2+1}}+c\).

115.subtopic: Algebraic Equations, Locus, and Cube Roots

116.solution: For \(x^2+y^2=36\), \(a=6\). Slope of \(5x+y=2\) is \(-5\), so required slope \(=\dfrac15\). Tangents: \(y=mx\pm\sqrt{a^2(1+m^2)}\Rightarrow y=\dfrac x5\pm6\sqrt{1+\tfrac1{25}}\Rightarrow x-5y\pm6\sqrt{26}=0\).

117.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
117.solution: \(\sin A=n\sin(A+2B)\Rightarrow\dfrac{\sin(A+2B)+\sin A}{\sin(A+2B)-\sin A}=\dfrac{1+n}{1-n}\) (componendo-dividendo). LHS \(=\dfrac{2\sin(A+B)\cos B}{2\cos(A+B)\sin B}=\dfrac{\tan(A+B)}{\tan B}\). Hence \(\tan(A+B)=\dfrac{1+n}{1-n}\tan B\).

118.solution: Linear dependence requires the determinant of the three vectors to vanish: \(\begin{vmatrix}p+1&-3&p\\p&p+1&-3\\-3&p&p+1\end{vmatrix}=0\). Expanding gives \(p^3+6p^2+6p-13=0=(p-1)(p^2+7p+13)\). The quadratic has discriminant \(49-52<0\), so the only integral value is \(p=1\): exactly \(1\) value.

119.solution: \(\sqrt{\tan x}+\sqrt{\cot x}=\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x\cos x}}=\sqrt2\,\dfrac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{1-(\sin x-\cos x)^2}}\). Put \(t=\sin x-\cos x\): \(I=\sqrt2\int_{-1}^{0}\dfrac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}=\sqrt2[\sin^{-1}t]_{-1}^0=\sqrt2\cdot\dfrac{\pi}2=\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt2}\).

120.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines

121.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
121.solution: For the ellipse \(a=5,b=3,e=\dfrac45\), foci \((\pm4,0)\). For the hyperbola with \(e'=2\): \(ae'=4\Rightarrow a=2\), \(b^2=a^2(e'^2-1)=4(3)=12\). Equation: \(\dfrac{x^2}4-\dfrac{y^2}{12}=1\).

122.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions

123.solution: \(\dfrac{dP}{dt}=-kP\Rightarrow\log\dfrac PN=-kt\). At \(t=1,\ P=\dfrac N2\Rightarrow k=\log2\). For \(P=\dfrac N{10}\) (90% lost): \(\log10=t\log2\Rightarrow t=\log_2 10\) hours.

124.stemOverride: If a random variable \(X\) has p.d.f. \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{ax^{2}}{2}+bx & ,\text{ if }1\le x\le 3\\ 0 & ,\text{ otherwise}\end{cases}\) and \(f(2)=2\), then the values of \(a\) and \(b\) are, respectively

125.solution: Let \(\overline m=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k\). \(\overline m\times\overline q=\overline r\times\overline q\) gives \(y-z=-10,\ x-z=-3,\ x-y=7\). With \(\overline m\cdot\overline p=2x+z=0\): \(z=x+3,\ 2x+x+3=0\Rightarrow x=-1,\ z=2,\ y=-8\). So \(\overline m=-\hat i-8\hat j+2\hat k\).

126.solution: Direction of the line of shortest distance \(=\bar b_1\times\bar b_2=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\-3&4&2\\-1&2&0\end{vmatrix}\parallel(2,1,1)\). Solving for the feet, \(P\equiv(1,-2,3)\) and \(Q\equiv(-3,-4,1)\); the line is \(\dfrac{x+3}2=\dfrac{y+4}1=\dfrac{z-1}1\). Since \((1,\alpha,\beta)\) lies on it, \(\alpha=-2,\ \beta=3\), so \(\alpha+\beta=1\).

127.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions
127.solution: Line 1 (intersection of \(x-3y-4=0,\ 4y-z+5=0\)) has direction \((3,1,4)\); line 2 (\(x+3y-11=0,\ 2y-z+6=0\)) has direction \((-3,1,2)\). \(\cos\theta\propto(3)(-3)+(1)(1)+(4)(2)=0\Rightarrow\theta=\dfrac{\pi}2\).

128.solution: Area with diagonals \(\bar d_1,\bar d_2\) is \(\dfrac12|\bar d_1\times\bar d_2|\). \((\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k)\times(2\hat i+3\hat j+\alpha\hat k)=(-\alpha-6)\hat i-(\alpha-4)\hat j+5\hat k\). Then \(\dfrac12\sqrt{(\alpha+6)^2+(\alpha-4)^2+25}=\dfrac{\sqrt{93}}2\Rightarrow2\alpha^2+4\alpha-16=0\Rightarrow(\alpha+4)(\alpha-2)=0\Rightarrow\alpha=-4,2\).

129.solution: From the graph the bounding lines are \(L_1:y-x=1\), \(L_2:2x+5y=10\) and \(L_3:x+y=1\). The shaded region lies on the non-origin side of \(L_1\) (so \(y-x\ge1\)) and of \(L_3\) (so \(x+y\ge1\)), and on the origin side of \(L_2\) (so \(2x+5y\le10\)), with \(x,y\ge0\).

130.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
130.solution: \(xy+2x+2y+4=(x+2)(y+2)=0\), giving lines \(x=-2,\ y=-2\). With \(x+y+2=0\) the vertices are \(A(-2,-2),B(0,-2),C(-2,0)\), a right angle at \(A\). Circumradius \(=\dfrac12 BC=\dfrac12\cdot2\sqrt2=\sqrt2\) units.

131.solution: Let \(y=x^{(x^x)}\Rightarrow\log y=x^x\log x\). Differentiating, \(\dfrac1y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{x-1}+\log x\cdot\dfrac{d}{dx}x^x=x^{x-1}+x^x\log x(1+\log x)\). Hence \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x^{(x^x)}\big[x^{x-1}+x^x\log x(1+\log x)\big]\).

132.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums
132.solution: Rewriting, \(\tan^{-1}\!\dfrac{x-\frac2x}{5+\frac8{x^2}}=\tan^{-1}\!\left(x-\dfrac2x\right)\Rightarrow\dfrac{x-\frac2x}{5+\frac8{x^2}}=x-\dfrac2x\). Either \(x-\dfrac2x=0\Rightarrow x^2=2\Rightarrow x=\pm\sqrt2\) (two solutions), or \(5+\dfrac8{x^2}=1\Rightarrow x^2=-2\) (impossible). So there are \(2\) solutions.

133.solution: Put \(x=\tan\theta\) in \(y=\tan^{-1}\!\dfrac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}x=\dfrac\theta2\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=\dfrac12\). Put \(x=\sin\theta\) in \(z=\tan^{-1}\!\dfrac{2x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{1-2x^2}=2\theta\Rightarrow\dfrac{dz}{d\theta}=2\). Hence \(\dfrac{dy}{dz}=\dfrac{1/2}{2}=\dfrac14\) (independent of the point).

134.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition
134.solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{9\cos\theta}{-9\sin\theta}=-\cot\theta\); slope of normal \(=\tan\theta\). Normal: \(y-9\sin\theta=\tan\theta\,[x-9(1+\cos\theta)]\Rightarrow x\sin\theta-y\cos\theta=9\sin\theta\). The point \((9,0)\) satisfies this for all \(\theta\).

136.subtopic: Negation, Equivalence, Tautology, and Switch Circuits
136.solution: From the circuit the upper branch is \(S_1\) in series with \(S_2\) parallel \(S_3\): \(p\wedge(q\vee r)\); the lower branch is \(S_3,S_2,S_1\) in series: \(p\wedge q\wedge r\). The branches are in parallel: \([p\wedge(q\vee r)]\vee(p\wedge q\wedge r)=p\wedge[(q\vee r)\vee(q\wedge r)]=p\wedge(q\vee r)\) (absorption).

139.solution: Each vector perpendicular to the sum of the other two gives \(\bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar b\cdot\bar c+\bar a\cdot\bar c=0\). Then \(|\bar a+\bar b+\bar c|^2=|\bar a|^2+|\bar b|^2+|\bar c|^2=25+144+169=338\), so \(|\bar a+\bar b+\bar c|=\sqrt{338}\).

140.solution: With square base side \(x\) and height \(h\), \(x^2h=4000\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{4000}{x^2}\). Surface area (open tank) \(A=x^2+4xh=x^2+\dfrac{16000}x\); \(A'=2x-\dfrac{16000}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow x^3=8000\Rightarrow x=20\). Then \(h=\dfrac{4000}{400}=10\). Side \(20\) cm, height \(10\) cm.

141.solution: A number is divisible by \(25\) if its last two digits are \(00,25,50,75\). From \(\{1,\dots,7\}\) without repetition, only \(25\) and \(75\) are possible. For each, the first two digits are chosen in \(5\times4=20\) ways. Total \(=20+20=40\).

142.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms
142.solution: \(\int e^{2x}\dfrac{\sin2x\cos2x-1}{\sin^2 2x}\,dx=\int e^{2x}(\cot2x-\operatorname{cosec}^2 2x)\,dx\). Put \(2x=t\): \(\dfrac12\int e^t(\cot t-\operatorname{cosec}^2 t)\,dt=\dfrac12 e^t\cot t+c=\dfrac12 e^{2x}\cot2x+c\).

143.subtopic: Basic Probability — Events, Conditional, and Complement
143.solution: One black, two white across the three urns. \(P(B_1W_2W_3)=\dfrac35\cdot\dfrac35\cdot\dfrac15=\dfrac9{125}\); \(P(W_1B_2W_3)=\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac15=\dfrac4{125}\); \(P(W_1W_2B_3)=\dfrac25\cdot\dfrac35\cdot\dfrac45=\dfrac{24}{125}\). Sum \(=\dfrac{37}{125}\).

144.subtopic: Sequences and Series — AP, HP, Logarithmic and Power Sums
144.solution: Concurrency: \(\begin{vmatrix}1&2a&a\\1&3b&b\\1&4c&c\end{vmatrix}=0\) gives \(2ac=ab+bc\Rightarrow\dfrac2b=\dfrac1a+\dfrac1c\). Hence \(a,b,c\) are in Harmonic progression.

147.solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sin\dfrac{x-y}2-\sin\dfrac{x+y}2=-2\cos\dfrac x2\sin\dfrac y2\). So \(\operatorname{cosec}\dfrac y2\,dy=-2\cos\dfrac x2\,dx\). Integrating: \(2\log\tan\dfrac y4=-4\sin\dfrac x2+c_1\Rightarrow\log\tan\dfrac y4=c-2\sin\dfrac x2\).

148.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

150.solution: \(\overline{PQ}=\hat i+3\hat j-\hat k\), line direction \(\bar b=\hat i+2\hat j+2\hat k\). Projection \(=\left|\dfrac{\overline{PQ}\cdot\bar b}{|\bar b|}\right|=\dfrac{|1+6-2|}{\sqrt{1+4+4}}=\dfrac53\).
